rewrites.prompt: A market research agency in Windhoek proposes raising a survey from 400 to 1 600 respondents, all interviewed at the same shopping centre on Saturday mornings. Explain one limitation of simply increasing the size of the sample.
rewrites.canonical_answer: A larger sample reduces sampling error, but it does not remove bias. On the approximate rule that the margin of error is about 1 divided by the square root of the sample size, moving from 400 to 1 600 respondents quadruples the fieldwork and its cost, and the margin narrows from about 5 to about 2.5 percentage points - half as wide for four times the work. And because the extra respondents are drawn the same way - one shopping centre, Saturday mornings - they repeat the same systematic difference from the wider population, so the narrower margin makes a distorted figure look more dependable than it is.
marking_guidance: 1 mark (AO1): the limitation identified - a larger sample narrows sampling error but leaves bias untouched.
2 marks (application): developed for the agency - four times the cost for a margin that halves, and the same shopping-centre bias reproduced; 1 mark if not carried into the context.
A developed limitation: carried one step further, because it leads to a biased figure that looks more dependable.
rewrites.why: State is not used on the current AS papers; 'state and develop' reworded to Explain at 3 marks, with a context supplied so the limitation can be applied.
